## Data

```{r}
#| label: load-pkgs
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data-1

super_bowl_data_1 <- read.csv("data/super-bowl-dataset-1.csv", col.names = c( "index", "game", "date", "winning_team", "winning_team_points", "winning_team_conference", "score", "losing_team", "losing_team_points", "losing_team_conference", "venue", "city", "attendance", "network", "avg_us_viewers", "rating", "share", "cost_per_30_sec_ad", "notes"))

```

```{r}
#| label: tidying-dataset-1

super_bowl_data_1 <- super_bowl_data_1 |>
  mutate(date = mdy(date)) |> 
  select(-index, -winning_team_conference, -losing_team_conference, -venue, -city, -notes) |> 
  mutate(avg_us_viewers = as.numeric(avg_us_viewers))

```

```{r}
#| label: plot-1

ggplot(super_bowl_data_1, aes(x = date, y = avg_us_viewers)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "5 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-06, suffix = " mil")) +
  labs(
    title = "Average U.S Television Viewers over Time",
    caption = "",
    x = "Date of Super Bowl",
    y = "Average U.S Television Viewers"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
#| label: plot-2

ggplot(super_bowl_data_1, aes(x = (winning_team_points - losing_team_points), y = cost_per_30_sec_ad, color = network)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Cost of 30 second Advertisement by Point Differential across Networks",
    caption = "",
    x = "Point Differential",
    y = "Cost of 30 second Advertisement",
    color = "Network"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar(scale = 1e-06, suffix = " mil")) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
#| label: plot-3

ggplot(super_bowl_data_1, aes(x = avg_us_viewers, y = cost_per_30_sec_ad, color = network)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Cost of a 30 second Ad based on Average U.S Viewers by Network",
    caption = "",
    x = "Average U.S Viewers (in millions)",
    y = "Cost of 30 second Advertisement (in millions of $)",
    color = "Network"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-06)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar(scale = 1e-06)) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
#| label: plot-4

ggplot(super_bowl_data_1, aes(x = (winning_team_points + losing_team_points), y = (winning_team_points - losing_team_points))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    caption = "",
    x = "Total Points",
    y = "Point Difference"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
#| label: calculating-correlation

super_bowl_data_1 |> 
  summarize(
    r = cor((winning_team_points + losing_team_points), (winning_team_points - losing_team_points)),
    r2 = r ^ 2,
    sx = sd((winning_team_points + losing_team_points), na.rm = TRUE),
    sy = sd((winning_team_points - losing_team_points), na.rm = TRUE),
    b1 = r * sy / sx
)

```

## Analysis
**Hypothesis 1**


**Hypothesis 2**
The second hypothesis guiding this project was that there would be no relationship between margin of victory and total points scored with our H₁ being the inverse, yielding a significant relationship. This analysis will use plot 4. Merely glancing at plot 4, there appears to be no relationship between the two variables. The scatterplot appears to be non-linear with a weak positive correlation. Our summary statistics table confirms this: our correlation coefficient (R value) is 0.280 which indicates a very low, positive relationship between the two variables.
